findings.claim: WA1-TRUTH's apex_port_signature artifact reports NULL port types on H22.0.400 (arity is correct, 'type' is null for every port). Root cause: probes.py _ports() calls _safe_str(p.name)/_safe_str(p.type_name), and _safe_str(fn) does str(fn()) -- it CALLS its argument, but p.name/p.type_name are string properties, so fn() raises and null is recorded. Downstream: the type set CANNOT be harvested from that artifact; consumers must read types from Graph.portTypeName(port_id) instead (as this leg does).
findings.anchor: wa1-truth runs/apex_basic_20260817_122650/apex_truth_22.0.400.json (e.g. Add<Matrix4> ports type:null); root cause at wa1-truth harness/autoresearch/probes.py:152 (_safe_str) + :1159-1160 (_safe_str(p.name)/(p.type_name))
findings.owner: WA1-TRUTH (their file; not fixed here -- flagged)

findings.claim: APEX wire typing is EXACT-match on 22.0.400. Graph.addWire is purely structural (always returns a wire; never type-checks); type checking is at Graph.resolveTypes()/errors(). Any mismatch -- even Int->Float -- rejects with 'Mismatched type: ...'. There is NO implicit wire coercion: over the full 21x21 product, 21 connect (exact-match diagonal) + 420 reject + 0 coerce. Coercion in APEX is explicit via Convert<A,B> callbacks (present in the catalog), not via a direct port-to-port wire.

@/$ resolution: $-forms expand and @-forms are literal in hscript_global (hou.text.expandString) and scene_node_parm (node string-parm eval); APEX graph parms store BOTH literally (typed data, no hscript expansion); the apex::invokegraph @attr binding is not measurable headless (needs a cooked geometry+graph invoke) -> UNKNOWN. $OS is context-dependent: 'Director' at session-global vs the node name ('font1') at node-context.

spawn.name: C2b: APEX explicit-coercion (Convert<A,B>) matrix - which cross-type conversions exist as callbacks
spawn.note: F2 established that a DIRECT wire never coerces. The complement of the wire matrix is the set of Convert<A,B> callbacks in apex.callbackRegistry() that DO provide explicit coercion. Probe kind apex_convert_matrix: for each ordered (A,B) in the wire-matrix type set, does 'Convert<A,B>' exist in callbackDefinitions()? Output a companion coercion table so W1 has both halves (wire=never-coerce, Convert=the explicit path). Pure registry-membership; deterministic; idempotent. Consumes the same declared type set.
